# FAQ {#sec-faq .unnumbered}

Here are some of the commonly-occurring issues that come up during this course and how to resolve them.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false}
### My exported map doesn't look as I expect

When you come to print or export a map from QGIS, the software does not simply send what is visible in the Print Layout to the printer. Instead, QGIS refers to the map item settings to define what is printed and how it should appear. If you made changes to one part of the composition since you last refreshed the screen, the map might not be printed as you expect. Making a layer visible in one map item will automatically make it visible (on printing or refreshing) in another unless you choose to lock the layers.

To make sure that you print or export only what you intend to, for each map item:

1. Compose the map item using the layers you need and their properties as you choose
2. Check the tickbox `lock layers for map item` which you will find under the `Item Properties` tab
3. Refresh the screen (`View` → `Refresh`) to make sure that everything looks as you want it to
4. Only then should you print or export
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false}
### My attributes table doesn't look as I expect

It's likely the attributes table view has been changed from 'table' to 'form' by mistake. To switch it back, click the `Switch to table view` icon (![](figs/SwitchToTableView.png){width=3%})
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false}
### The "Handle Bad Layers" window appears when I open a project 

If, when you open an existing project, you are presented with a message saying 'Handle Bad Layers', then your QGIS project cannot connect to some or all of the data layers that you have opened previously. This can happen if you inadvertently move or delete data files that are part of your project. The only way to recover is to put things back as they were, or to re-open the 'Bad Layers'.

Another possible cause for 'Bad Layers' is that OneDrive did not connect properly to your computer when you logged in. The best solution is to log out and in again.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false}
### I'm getting the error "One or more input features have invalid geometry"

Invalid geometry is when a vector layer breaks, such as when a polygon boundary crosses itself or a line has zero length. Invalid geometries can creep in when manipulating layers e.g. cropping roads to your map tile. 

To resolve invalid geometries:

1. Ensure the `Processing Toolbox` is visible by clicking the cog icon (![](figs/ProcessingToolbox.png){width=3%})
2. Search for `fix geometries`
3. Double-click on `Fix geometries`
4. Under the `Input layer` drop-down, select the offending vector layer
5. Click `Run` → `Close`

A new layer will be created, which looks identical to the original layer, with the broken geometries resolved. You can now proceed with your original workflow.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false}
### My "Processing" menu is missing

The 'Processing' menu is a QGIS plugin, so it's likely the plugin is missing on your project. 

To add it back in:

1. Click `Plugins` → `Manage and Install Plugins...`
2. Search for `processing`
3. Check the box next to `Processing`
4. Click `Close`

The 'Processing' menu should now be visible.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false}
### My work didn't save

The three most likely reasons are: 

1. You logged out of your PC before OneDrive had time to sync files correctly (i.e. move your data from the PC to the cloud). Always ensure there is a small tick next to your file in the browser window to confirm the file has been synced correctly. 
2. You saved the data 'locally' (i.e. on the PC) rather than on your OneDrive. You *may* be able to recover your files if you return to the exact PC you were using, and then save the data on your OneDrive. However, University PCs are wiped every Friday - so be quick!
3. You have saved the data on your OneDrive, but you can't remember where. Try finding the files under the 'Recent' icon on your browser, then save them somewhere more sensible.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false}
### How can I arrange map items perfectly on the print layout?

Use 'guides'. These allow you snap map items (e.g. the edge of a map) onto the line, aligning everything perfectly.

To add guides:

1. Click the `Guides` tab, or click `View` → `Show Guides` if they're not visible
2. Click the `Add new guide` icon (![](figs/AddANewGrid.png){width=3%})
3. Set the guide distance, which will be in mm from the top (horizontal guides) or left (vertical guides)
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false}
### One of my panels is missing, how do I get it back?

If a panel or toolbar is missing:

1. Click `View` → `Panels` or `Toolbars`
2. Select the relevant panel/toolbar
:::
